title: Hard-look review and the rulemaking record
shortTitle: Hard-look review and the rulemaking record
summary: Hard-look review tests whether an agency has explained a legally permissible choice in light of important evidence, objections, and alternatives.
notes:
Hard-look review is judicial examination of whether agency reasoning connects the record, the governing statute, and the choice made. The automobile-safety materials trace its development from APA §§ 553(c) and 706 as broad policy decisions increasingly received direct, pre-enforcement review. A statement of basis and purpose must disclose how the agency handled major issues; an agency need not answer every observation or use a trial’s findings format.

The record in informal rulemaking can include studies, comments, and other material without a trial-type hearing. Its existence does not trigger §§ 556–557. Contemporary explanatory materials can make the rationale intelligible, but the notes warn against relying on later litigation rationalizations or expecting the reviewing court to assemble a rationale itself. The statutory and institutional settings matter: APA review of an agency’s delegated choices demands explanations beyond the minimal constitutional rationality inquiry applied to legislation.
